# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Agent provenance and human review

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Create every agent-created ticket in the existing `Ticket Draft` status with exactly one existing workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group. The label records provenance and stays after approval.
- Select the label from the creating agent's known identity: `Created by Claude` for Claude, `Created by Codex` for Codex, or `Created by LLM` for any other agent or when its identity cannot be determined. Do not infer agent identity from the Linear account, ticket topic, or skill name. Do not use `Created by LLM` as a substitute when the correct agent-specific label is missing.
- `Ticket Draft` is in the Backlog category and means human ticket review is pending; it does not authorize implementation. The existing `Draft` status belongs to the Started category and is used by the PR workflow. Do not use it for ticket review or change its automation.
- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Obsidian work with no relevant project, leave the project empty and apply the existing `Obsidian plugin` label. Do not use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`; the Obsidian queue picks up unprojected issues by label (see DIS-617).
4. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Any project you select must exist, not be completed, canceled, archived, or trashed, and include the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one. Obsidian tickets that do belong to a real project still use that project, plus the `Obsidian plugin` label.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label. Always apply `Obsidian plugin` to Obsidian work, since it is how unprojected Obsidian tickets reach the queue.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft`, the required provenance label, or `Obsidian plugin` for Obsidian work is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project (omitted for unprojected Obsidian work), provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. For unprojected Obsidian work, confirm the project is empty and `Obsidian plugin` is applied. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

input.title: Make `Concept.source_local_id` NOT NULL
input.description:
## Problem

- The database accepts a Concept with no `source_local_id`. Sync can't find or update that row, but it still holds its name in the unique index on `(space_id, name)`. The real node with that name can then never be written.
- On 2026-11-03, 708 of 1432 Concepts in the discourse-graphs space had a NULL `source_local_id`, and they stopped Roam sync. ENG-2452 deleted them. Nothing stops new ones.
- The known cause is gone: Concepts stopped taking their identity from Content in January 2026. But `_local_concept_to_db_concept` still turns an empty `source_local_id` into NULL, and the schema accepts that row without an error. The bad row only shows up later, when a name collides.
- Now is the cheap moment. Production has no NULL rows, and the client sync code is likely to change a lot, so the protection belongs in the database.

## Solution

- Add a NOT NULL constraint on `Concept.source_local_id`, in the schema and in a migration.

## Done When

- The migration applies on a database with no NULL `source_local_id` Concepts, including production.
- Inserting a Concept with a NULL or empty `source_local_id` fails.
- In `upsert_concepts`, a row with a missing or empty `source_local_id` returns `-2` with a warning that names the column, and the other rows in the batch are still saved. A test covers this.
- The existing database test suite passes.

## Out of Scope

- `source_local_id` on Content and Document, which is also nullable.
- How a future web-created Concept gets its `source_local_id`. Web nodes will need one, but the id scheme isn't decided.
- Client-side handling of `-2` results in Roam or Obsidian sync.

## Notes

- Depends on ENG-2452 (Done). Before applying in production, check that no Concept has a NULL `source_local_id`. The migration fails otherwise.
- All Concept fixtures in the cucumber features already set `source_local_id`.
- The `(space_id, source_local_id)` index is declared `NULLS DISTINCT`, which is the Postgres default and is used across Concept, Content and Document. It doesn't matter once the column rejects NULL.
- Source: Roam issue candidate `0nLVRPvPo`.
- Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

Yes, it's the same pattern. Here's what I found:

- **Columns:** `source_local_id` is nullable on `Document` and on `Content`, as it was on `Concept`.
- **Indexes:** `document_space_and_local_id_idx` and `content_space_local_id_variant_content_type_idx` both declare `NULLS DISTINCT`. I can't see production, so one point is still unknown: whether Content or Document already has NULL-id rows there. The 708 Concepts had no Content, which tells us nothing either way. ---

**Title:** Make `source_local_id` NOT NULL on Concept, Content and Document

## Problem
- Concept, Content and Document all accept a row with no `source_local_id`. Their unique indexes on `source_local_id` declare `NULLS DISTINCT`, so any number of these rows can coexist. Sync can't find or update such a row.
- On Concept, such rows also hold their name in the `(space_id, name)` index. On 2026-11-03, 708 of them stopped Roam sync in the discourse-graphs space. ENG-2452 deleted them. Nothing stops new ones in any of the three tables.
- `_local_concept_to_db_concept` still turns an empty `source_local_id` into NULL, and the schema accepts the row without an error. The bad row only shows up later, when something collides.
- The client sync code is likely to change a lot, so the protection belongs in the database.

## Solution
- Add NOT NULL to `source_local_id` on Concept, Content and Document, in the schema and in a migration.
- Recreate their unique indexes that include `source_local_id` without `NULLS DISTINCT`.

## Done When
- Production has no Content or Document with a NULL `source_local_id`, or a separate cleanup ticket blocks this one.
- The migration applies on a database with no NULL `source_local_id` in the three tables, including production.
- Inserting a row with a NULL or empty `source_local_id` into any of the three tables fails.
- No unique index on these tables that includes `source_local_id` declares `NULLS DISTINCT`, in the schema or the migration.
- In `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`, a row with a missing or empty `source_local_id` returns an error value with a warning that names the column, and the other rows in the batch are still saved. Tests cover this.
- The existing database test suite passes.

## Out of Scope
- How a future web-created node gets its `source_local_id`. Web nodes will need one, but the id scheme isn't decided.
- Client-side handling of error results in Roam or Obsidian sync.

## Notes
- Depends on ENG-2452 (Done) for Concept.
- All Concept fixtures in the cucumber features already set `source_local_id`. Content and Document fixtures need the same check.
- Source: Roam issue candidate `0nLVRPvPo`.
- Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

I can't say they're safe yet. Deleting a Document cascades further than the Document itself:

1. Only Content references Document, through `Content_document_id_fkey`, which is `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
2. Deleting that Content then cascades to its embeddings, its `content_contributors` and its `FileReference` rows (assets). Content parts that point at it through `part_of_id` lose the link (SET NULL).
3. Every Content row has a non-null `source_local_id`. So if either Document has Content attached, deleting it would remove real, findable Content along with its embeddings and assets. That would be real data lost, not just a broken row.

So the question is whether those two Documents have any Content. Can you run this on production? It's read-only:

```sql
SELECT d.id, d.space_id, s.name AS space, d.url, d.created, d.last_modified,
       count(c.id) AS contents,
       count(c.id) FILTER (WHERE fr.content_id IS NOT NULL) AS with_assets
FROM public."Document" d
JOIN public."Space" s ON s.id = d.space_id
LEFT JOIN public."Content" c ON c.document_id = d.id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT 1 AS content_id FROM public."FileReference" f
                   WHERE (f.space_id, f.source_local_id, f.variant) = (c.space_id, c.source_local_id, c.variant)
                   LIMIT 1) fr ON true
WHERE d.source_local_id IS NULL
GROUP BY d.id, s.name;
```

How to read it:
- **`contents` = 0:** the delete removes only the Document, and it's safe.
- **`contents` > 0:** don't delete. Give the Document an id instead. If the Content's `source_local_id` is the page id, the Document's id is most likely that same value: `upsert_content` gives a Document its Content's id when the Document has none.

About `upsert_content`: if we're moving to `upsert_concepts` with embedded Content, then making `upsert_content` report errors properly isn't worth doing. I'll drop it from Done When and add a line to Out of Scope.

-- its own Document, the way upsert_content does today (content_as_document = true):
-- one Document per Content source_local_id, same id, created/last_modified/author from the Content.

INSERT INTO public."Document" (space_id, source_local_id, created, last_modified, author_id, content_type)
SELECT
    c.space_id,
    c.source_local_id,
    min(c.created),
    max(c.last_modified),
    coalesce(
        (array_agg(c.author_id ORDER BY c.id) FILTER (WHERE c.author_id IS NOT NULL))[1],

        WHEN 'Obsidian' THEN 'text/obsidian+markdown'

FROM public."Content" AS c
JOIN public."Document" AS d ON d.id = c.document_id
JOIN public."Space" AS s ON s.id = c.space_id
WHERE c.document_id = 21212
GROUP BY c.space_id, c.source_local_id, d.author_id, s.platform

SET document_id = nd.id
FROM public."Document" AS nd

Don't delete Document 21212. That would cascade-delete its 72 Content rows. I wrote a repair script that gives each of those Content rows its own Document, which is what sync would build today.

**Why 72 rows are still on it:** current sync calls `upsert_concepts` with `content_as_document = true`. That gives every Content its own Document with the same `source_local_id`. The upsert's conflict clause also replaces `document_id` with the new Document. So whenever megacoglab re-sent one of those nodes, it moved off 21212. The 72 still attached are nodes that haven't been re-sent since May 2025. Either they haven't changed since, or they're gone from the graph. That's also why they have different ids: each is a separate node that the early sync code put in one shared Document.

**The repair** is at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maparent-OpenSource-discourse-graph/4f74a5b0-e4f9-4990-8212-b5c1f88251d8/scratchpad/repair_document_21212.sql`. Inside one transaction it:
1. Creates one Document for each distinct Content `source_local_id`. It uses the Content's earliest `created`, latest `last_modified` and author. If no Content has an author, it falls back to 21212's author. The content type comes from the space's platform. Ids that already have a Document are skipped.
2. Points each Content at the Document with its own id.
3. Prints two counts, both of which should be 0: Content still on 21212, and other Documents with a NULL id.
4. Deletes 21212.

The script ends without `COMMIT`, so you can check the counts and then commit or roll back. I checked the column names against the schema but haven't run the script anywhere.

If some of those 72 nodes no longer exist in Roam, their Content stays as stale rows. It would be the same if sync had moved them. That's the missing-delete-cascades problem, not this ticket's.

Once production has no NULL-id Documents, the first Done When item can simply say that ENG-2452, your deletion of Document 21177 and this repair cleared all three tables. input.title: Make `source_local_id` NOT NULL on Concept, Content and Document
input.description:
## Problem

- Concept, Content and Document all accept a row with no `source_local_id`. Their unique indexes on `source_local_id` declare `NULLS DISTINCT`, so any number of these rows can coexist. Sync can't find or update such a row.
- On Concept, such rows also hold their name in the `(space_id, name)` index. On 2026-11-03, 708 of them stopped Roam sync in the discourse-graphs space. Nothing stops new ones in any of the three tables.
- `_local_concept_to_db_concept` still turns an empty `source_local_id` into NULL, and the schema accepts the row without an error. The bad row only shows up later, when something collides.
- The client sync code is likely to change a lot, so the protection belongs in the database.

## Solution

- Add NOT NULL to `source_local_id` on Concept, Content and Document, in the schema and in a migration.
- Recreate their unique indexes that include `source_local_id` without `NULLS DISTINCT`.

## Done When

- The migration applies on production and on a fresh local database.
- Inserting a row with a NULL or empty `source_local_id` into any of the three tables fails.
- No unique index on these tables that includes `source_local_id` declares `NULLS DISTINCT`, in the schema or the migration.
- In `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`, a row with a missing or empty `source_local_id` returns an error value with a warning that names the column, and the other rows in the batch are still saved. Tests cover this.
- The existing database test suite passes.

## Out of Scope

- How a future web-created node gets its `source_local_id`. Web nodes will need one, but the id scheme isn't decided.
- Client-side handling of error results in Roam or Obsidian sync.

## Notes

- As of 2026-11-13, production has no NULL `source_local_id` in the three tables. ENG-2452 deleted the 708 Concepts. Two Documents remained, both created in May 2025 by pre-release code. Document 21177 (discourse-dev-graph) had no Content and was deleted. Document 21212 (megacoglab) held 72 Content rows; each now has its own Document with its `source_local_id`, as current sync builds them, and 21212 was deleted.
- All Concept fixtures in the cucumber features already set `source_local_id`. Content and Document fixtures need the same check.
- `upsert_content` is expected to give way to `upsert_concepts` with embedded Content, but that move isn't scheduled.
- Source: Roam issue candidate `0nLVRPvPo`.
- Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style
